chunks: Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Shu'ayb al-Jawhari (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: 'Isa ibn Muhammad al-'Alawi narrated to us. He said: Abu 'Amr Ahmad ibn Abi Hazim al-Ghifari narrated to us. He said: 'Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Sharik, from Rukayn ibn al-Rabi', from al-Qasim ibn Hassan, from Zayd ibn Thabit who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Surely, I am leaving among you the two weighty things: the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and my progeny, my Ahl al-Bayt. Verily, they are the two vicegerents after me. They shall never separate until they return to me at the Pond.'

key_terms.أَهْل الْبَيْت: Ahl al-Bayt — the People of the House; the Prophet's household, in Shia understanding comprising the fourteen infallibles
key_terms.الثَّقَلَيْن: The Two Weighty Things — the Quran and the Ahl al-Bayt; the dual form of thaqal (something precious/weighty)
key_terms.الْحَوْض: The Pond (al-Kawthar) — the Prophet's pool in the Hereafter, to which he will welcome believers on the Day of Resurrection
key_terms.الْخَلِيفَتَان: The two vicegerents/successors — this word explicitly designates them as political and religious authorities after the Prophet
key_terms.عِتْرَة: Progeny/kindred; specifically refers to the Prophet's closest kin and household

ai.seo_question: What is the Hadith al-Thaqalayn and what are the Two Weighty Things the Prophet left behind?
ai.summary: This is a rendition of the famous Hadith al-Thaqalayn (the Hadith of the Two Weighty Things), here transmitted through the companion Zayd ibn Thabit. The Prophet (s) declared before his community that he was leaving behind two inseparable authorities — the Quran and his Ahl al-Bayt — designating them jointly as his successors. This version notably uses the word 'khalifahtan' (two vicegerents/successors), a term carrying explicit political and religious authority, underscoring the Shia doctrinal position on the Imamate. The hadith is widely attested across both Sunni and Shia sources with some variation in wording.
